source: To be clear, across 18 paired runs, the mean time difference (A minus B) was −3 ms (95% CI −8 to 2 ms). This may potentially indicate faster runs with A, although the interval includes zero.
preserve: The mean difference is based on 18 paired runs.
A minus B is −3 ms. The 95% confidence interval extends from −8 to 2 ms.
The interval includes zero. Faster observed mean time does not establish a faster method overall.
near_miss: Across 18 paired runs, A was conclusively faster than B by 3 ms (95% CI −8 to 2 ms).

source: In an observational study at two campuses, longer gaps between buses were associated with lower weekday ridership. It is important to note that weekend ridership was not measured.
preserve: The study is observational and covers two campuses.
The weekday result is an association between longer gaps and lower ridership.
Weekend ridership was unmeasured. Its response is unknown.
near_miss: At two campuses, longer gaps between buses reduced weekday ridership and had no effect on weekends.
